Newgen Software Technologies is a company based in New Delhi, India, where Gopal Sharma works as a Senior Data Scientist. The company is involved in Generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), GraphRAG, and LLM systems.
Generative AI refers to a class of artificial intelligence technologies capable of generating new content, such as text, images, or data, based on learned patterns and inputs.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a method that combines information retrieval with generative models to enhance the accuracy and relevance of generated outputs by incorporating external knowledge sources.

GraphRAG is a method that extends retrieval-augmented generation by utilizing graph structures to represent and retrieve knowledge, enabling more effective and context-aware information retrieval and generation.

LLM systems refer to large language model systems, which are advanced artificial intelligence models capable of understanding and generating human-like text based on extensive training on large datasets.

Multi-hop GraphRAG is a project in which Gopal Sharma designed a bidirectional meet-in-the-middle graph search to answer multi-hop questions over a LightRAG knowledge graph, improving accuracy and correct-path selection.
The LightRAG knowledge graph is a dataset containing 52,474 nodes and 60,475 edges, used in the Multi-hop GraphRAG project to answer multi-hop questions.
Breadth-First Search is a graph traversal algorithm used to explore or search tree or graph data structures level by level, starting from the root node.
Embedding filtering is a technique used to filter or refine search results by comparing embeddings, which are numerical representations of data points, to identify the most relevant candidates.

Query routing is a project in which Gopal Sharma explored the effectiveness of query decomposition as a strategy for improving accuracy in answering complex questions, particularly in the context of the HotpotQA dataset.
HotpotQA questions are a dataset of complex, multi-hop questions designed to evaluate the ability of models to answer questions that require reasoning across multiple pieces of information.

answer accuracy is a performance metric used in the evaluation plan of the Claude Desktop project to measure how accurately the system can provide correct answers to questions.
An anchor is a key node in GraphWalk-RAG that is used to seed answers from the reachable set and dominate the question's embedding.
The reachable set refers to the set of nodes that can be reached from an anchor in the graph. It is used in GraphWalk-RAG to find the gold answer with high recall.

Reranking is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where answer candidates are ranked based on joined high-level keywords instead of the original question, improving the position of the gold answer in the ranking.
Cosine similarity is a metric used in GraphWalk-RAG for initial ranking of answer candidates, but it can be overwritten by a cross-encoder during reranking.

cross-encoder is a type of model used for reranking in the Claude Desktop project, which is noted to be computationally intensive on CPU and thus recommended to be used on GPU or with a smaller variant.
A distance shell refers to a layer of nodes at a certain distance from the anchor in GraphWalk-RAG. Each shell is given its own slots to avoid missing candidates due to depth blindness.
K Chains refers to a concept in GraphWalk-RAG where the reader is allowed to choose among K chains, acting as a better final-hop judge than cosine similarity.

Quickstart is a process described in the documentation for GraphWalk-RAG that provides instructions for installing the package, setting up the API key, and running various commands to build, verify, and ask questions using the system.

GraphWalk-RAG Verify is a process that checks if the provenance of the graph is intact across all six stores.
GraphWalk-RAG Ask is a process that allows users to ask questions based on the built graph, with options for guided or router modes to handle complex queries.
GraphWalk-RAG Export-Neo4j is a process that exports the built graph to Neo4j, requiring configuration of the Neo4j URI, user, and password.
Regulation is an entity type used in GraphWalk-RAG to classify certain nodes in the graph, representing legal or regulatory frameworks.
Section is an entity type used in GraphWalk-RAG to classify certain nodes in the graph, representing sections of documents or regulations.
Institution is an entity type used in GraphWalk-RAG to classify certain nodes in the graph, representing organizations or institutions.
Requirement is an entity type used in GraphWalk-RAG to classify certain nodes in the graph, representing specific requirements or conditions.
Guided Mode is a technology used in GraphWalk-RAG's ask process, providing assistance in answering complex questions by following a guided approach.
Router Mode is a technology used in GraphWalk-RAG's ask process, which decomposes queries on abstention and uses a LightRAG mix for question answering.

LLM Model is a technology used in GraphWalk-RAG for specifying the model to be used from the local language model server, such as Qwen/Qwen3-14B.
Workdir is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the directory used for storing intermediate files and outputs during the build and processing of the graph.
Entity Types are concepts in GraphWalk-RAG that define the categories of nodes in the graph, such as Regulation, Section, Institution, and Requirement.
Provenance is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the origin or source of the data in the graph, ensuring that the data's integrity and traceability are maintained across all stores.
Answer Recall is a metric used in GraphWalk-RAG to measure the proportion of correct answers retrieved from the graph, with the anchor's reachable set achieving 99% recall.
Cosine Order is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where answer candidates are initially ranked based on cosine similarity, which can be overwritten by a cross-encoder during reranking.
Cross-Encoder Saturation is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where the performance of the cross-encoder diminishes with a larger rerank pool, leading to potential degradation in answer quality.
Depth-Blind Top-M is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where the top-M candidates are selected without considering depth, which can result in missing candidates if the depth is not properly accounted for.
Generic Connectors are concepts in GraphWalk-RAG that refer to nodes with high degrees, which are identified as sources of distractor paths and are avoided using the Hub Guard process.

Reader Judgment is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where the reader is allowed to choose among K chains, acting as a better final-hop judge than cosine similarity, leading to improved accuracy in answer selection.
K Chains Selection is a process in GraphWalk-RAG that allows the reader to choose among K chains, improving the final answer selection by leveraging human judgment.
Gold Answer is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the correct answer to a question, which is often found in the anchor's reachable set with high probability.
Anchor Neighbors is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the nodes directly connected to the anchor, which are pulled in during the reranking process to improve the gold answer's position.
Rerank Pool is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the set of answer candidates considered during the reranking process, with a larger pool potentially leading to cross-encoder saturation.
Question Embedding is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the vector representation of a question, which is dominated by the anchor and used for retrieval purposes.
Distractor Paths are concepts in GraphWalk-RAG that refer to incorrect or irrelevant paths in the graph that can lead to incorrect answers and are avoided using the Hub Guard process.
Answer Position is a metric used in GraphWalk-RAG to measure the rank of the gold answer among all candidates, with reranking significantly improving its position in some cases.
Depth-Blindness is a concept in GraphWalk-RAG that refers to the lack of consideration for depth in selecting top-M candidates, which can lead to missing valid candidates if not addressed.
Node Degree is a metric used in GraphWalk-RAG to measure the number of connections a node has, with nodes of degree greater than 150 being avoided due to their role as generic connectors.

Entity Extraction is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where entities are identified and classified based on their types, such as Regulation, Section, Institution, and Requirement, to build the graph structure.
Relationship Extraction is a process in GraphWalk-RAG where relationships between entities are identified and recorded to form the graph structure, enabling efficient question answering.

A policy refers to a strategy or method applied in decision-making processes, such as the "single-pass mix" or "always decompose (self-ask)" policies mentioned in the context of accuracy and decomposition usage.
Accuracy is a metric used to evaluate the performance of a system, measured as a percentage. In the given context, it quantifies the correctness of responses generated by different policies.
Decomposition is a process where a complex question is broken down into simpler sub-questions. It is described as a "rescue, not a default" and is applied selectively based on policies.
Single-pass `mix` is a policy that processes questions in a single pass without decomposition. It achieves an accuracy of 70.2% and does not use decomposition.
Always decompose (self-ask) is a policy that always breaks down questions into sub-questions. It achieves an accuracy of 62.8% and uses decomposition on all questions.
Oracle is a policy that selects the best response from all possible options, achieving an accuracy of 81.5%. It is considered the "best of both" and does not have a defined decomposition percentage.
The regulatory corpus is a dataset containing 371 regulatory documents (17,326 pages) and 101 questions with gold pages. It is used for evaluating the performance of graph-based systems.
Doc recall @5 / @10 / @20 is a metric that measures the proportion of relevant documents retrieved at the top 5, 10, and 20 positions. It is reported as 0.804 / 0.865 / 0.927.
Evidence-page recall @20 is a metric that measures the proportion of relevant evidence pages retrieved at the top 20 positions. It is reported as 0.85.
Fully on-prem rebuild refers to the process of rebuilding the graph using on-premises infrastructure, such as Qwen3 on vLLM and bge-m3, as opposed to cloud-based builds.
Cloud build refers to the process of constructing the graph using cloud-based infrastructure. It is compared to the fully on-prem rebuild in terms of performance metrics.
Latency is a metric that measures the time taken for a process to complete. In this context, it includes 8.7 seconds for retrieval and 4.5 seconds for answering.
Unguided walk is a process where navigation through the graph is not directed, leading to drifting through hub entities. It is less effective for the regulatory corpus.
Hub entities are highly connected nodes in a graph. In the regulatory corpus, 19% of top-20 path edges were about the question, with only 43% on the first hop and 10% from the second hop.
The HotpotQA graph is a dataset used for evaluating multi-hop reasoning systems. It has a mean degree of 2.3 and a max degree of 211.
The regulatory graph is a dataset derived from the regulatory corpus. It has a mean degree of 4.71 and a max degree of 5,830, with the regulator itself being the highest-degree node.
Nodes above the hub guard are entities with a degree greater than 150. In the HotpotQA graph, there are 2 such nodes, while in the regulatory graph, there are 88.
Isolated nodes are entities with no connections to other nodes. In the HotpotQA graph, they make up 3.1% of the nodes, while in the regulatory graph, they make up 11.0%.
